newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares struggle in tight range despite dlr.
newsitem.headline: German shares struggle in tight range despite dlr.

text.p: German shares were seen range-bound by wide investor scepticism over the viability of further gains and thus not exploiting the strong move ahead in the dollar as much as has been the case in the past.

The IBIS-DAX index of electronic trade rose 13.72 points to 3,371.29 on poor early volumes, a subdued reaction to the weekend surge of the dollar to 56-month highs against the mark. June DAX futures rose 14 points to 3,373.5.
"There is a high degree of scepticism in the market," said one trader, noting continued concern over a possible U.S.-led credit tightening.

The dollar is now seen rising, in the mid- to longer-term possibly up to 1.80 marks, after a Group of Seven communique at the weekend was interpreted as not expressing dissatisfaction with the current high value of the dollar.

Export-sensitive German stocks clearly benefited most from the dollar gains, with chemical groups Hoechst and Bayer leading trading volumes and gaining 1.01 marks to 67.10 and 40 pfennigs to 68.30 respectively.
Daimler gained 1.10 marks to 127.40 on a report of plans for heavy job cuts and a separate British newspaper report of a merger between Airbus and U.S.-based Lockheed.
Daimler-Benz Aerospace is one of four European partners in the Airbus plane-making consortium. London-based equity analysts contacted on Sunday said they were treating the report sceptically.
Car-maker Volkswagen gained 13.50 marks to 1,086.50 after its chairman Ferdinand Piech was quoted saying he was aiming to quadruple pre-tax profits by 2000.
Piech was quoted in the "Focus" news magazine as saying the group would save costs by reducing the number of basic structures on which future VW cars would be built.
Dealers said the start of dealings in finance, savings and insurance group BHW Holding later today would probably be one of the day's trading focuses.
BHW said at the weekend it would be pricing its shares at 26 marks each, towards the top of the range set for the bookbuilding process, and that its issue had been 14.5 times oversubscribed.
